subject: Nanotechnology
title: Hierarchical Self-Assembly
description: A micro-lesson that makes Hierarchical Self-Assembly usable.

hook.text: Bone builds across scales — minerals in collagen fibrils in lamellae in osteons. Nature assembles hierarchically.

buildup.text: Hierarchical self-assembly means small units form first, then those units assemble into larger structures, and so on.

discovery.text: Each level uses different interactions — hydrogen bonds at the molecular level, electrostatics at the mesoscale.

twist.text: Engineering multi-level assembly is hard — conditions that favor one level may disrupt another.

climax.text: Peptide amphiphiles self-assemble into nanofibers that form hydrogels — mimicking the hierarchy of natural tissue.

punchline.text: One level of order is easy — stacking levels of order is how nature builds complexity.

quiz.question: What is hierarchical self-assembly?
options: Assembly that only works at one size scale
Small units assemble first, then those units form larger structures across multiple length scales
A process where larger structures break down into smaller ones
